title: Kinematics of Inverse Compton Scattering from Dirac Carriers in Graphene
authors: Dar Faheem Ul Haq, Naveed Ahmad Shah, SSZ Ashraf
abstract: We examine the kinematics of Compton and inverse Compton scattering by Dirac carriers in graphene. Unlike photons in vacuum, which propagate at the speed of light c, graphene carriers have a characteristic velocity vF, with vF much less than c. This difference means that the standard Compton scattering formula cannot be applied to graphene simply by replacing c with vF. We first examine Compton-like scattering for a gapless Dirac carrier initially at the Dirac point and for a gapped carrier at the band edge, both corresponding to zero in-plane momentum. We then consider scattering from an energetic gapless Dirac carrier. By combining energy conservation with the graphene dispersion and in-plane momentum conservation, we obtain a quadratic equation for the scattered photon energy within the model considered. This relation is the main kinematic result of the work. We identify inverse Compton-like scattering by the transfer of energy from the carrier to the photon, subject to the simultaneous conservation of energy and in-plane momentum. We also discuss how this process differs kinematically from Doppler-shifted emission, Cerenkov-like radiation, harmonic generation, photon drag, and other nonlinear optical processes. Finally, we propose a time-resolved pump-probe arrangement in which the scattered photon spectrum is the primary observable, while time- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (TR-ARPES) provides an independent probe of the nonequilibrium carrier distribution. These results provide a kinematic framework for analysing inverse Compton-like scattering in graphene and for identifying the conditions under which energy can be transferred from energetic Dirac carriers to photons.
summary: This paper develops a kinematic framework to analyze Inverse Compton Scattering from Dirac carriers in graphene, recognizing that the low Fermi velocity ($v_F$) invalidates simple substitutions into standard scattering formulas. The main result is a derived quadratic equation governing the scattered photon energy, which is proposed to be measured using a time-resolved pump-probe setup coupled with TR-ARPES diagnostics.
main_problem: The paper investigates the kinematics of Inverse Compton Scattering (ICS) involving Dirac carriers in graphene, noting that standard scattering formulas fail because graphene carriers move at a characteristic velocity $v_F \ll c$.
main_result: The authors derive a specific quadratic kinematic relation for the scattered photon energy, establishing a framework to distinguish ICS from other nonlinear optical processes like Doppler shifts.
method: The derivation relies on combining energy conservation with the graphene's linear dispersion relation and in-plane momentum conservation, leading to a purely kinematic model.
model_or_system: The system is graphene, modeled by Dirac quasiparticles with a linear dispersion $E = v_F|\mathbf{\pi}|$. The analysis contrasts the effective 2+1 dimensional metric governed by $v_F$ against the vacuum metric governed by $c$.
key_observables: The scattered photon spectrum ($\hbar\omega_f, \mathbf{k}_{\gamma f}$) is the primary observable, complemented by time- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (TR-ARPES) to probe the transient carrier distribution.
important_parameters: The characteristic Fermi velocity $v_F$, the photon frequency ($\omega_i, \omega_f$), and the energy/momentum conservation laws are central.
main_assumptions: The work establishes a kinematic framework only; it does not provide the scattering rate or prove experimental detectability, requiring future work on matrix elements.
figures_summary: Figure 2 illustrates the proposed time-resolved pump-probe geometry: an ultrafast pump pulse creates carriers, which then undergo ICS with an incident photon, while a separate TR-ARPES probe measures the resulting non-equilibrium carrier distribution.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first identifying the failure of standard formulas, deriving the general kinematic relations for both gapless and gapped graphene, establishing the ICS signature ($\omega_f > \omega_i$ and $E_f < E_i$), and concluding with a detailed proposal for a time-resolved pump-probe experiment combining photon detection with TR-ARPES diagnostics.
why_interesting: This work is relevant to quantum optics and open quantum systems because it models energy and momentum transfer in a solid-state system (graphene) where the mediating quasiparticles have highly non-relativistic, linear dispersion relations, requiring specialized conservation laws beyond standard QED treatments.
